questions.q: In a painting, the artist wants the viewer to look at the main character first before noticing the background. The principle used to create this central focal point is called:
questions.explain: Dominance, also known as Emphasis, is used to make a specific part of an artwork stand out or attract the viewer's attention first. This area becomes the focal point.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: An artist creates a black-and-white charcoal drawing of a city street but uses bright yellow paint for a single taxi cab in the center. The taxi cab is an example of:
options: A focal point created by contrast
questions.explain: The bright colour against a dull, monochromatic background creates high contrast. This draws the eye immediately, making the taxi cab the focal point (an application of Dominance).
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: In relation to Dominance, what term describes the less important parts of a composition that fade into the background to help the focal point stand out?
questions.explain: Subordination is the counterpart to dominance (emphasis). The subordinate elements are intentionally made less visually interesting so that they do not compete with the dominant focal point.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
